title: Resume-quality A/B: Jev-prune vs generic summary
description:
WHAT: Run the resume-quality A/B that decides whether Jev-pruning beats generic summarization on real omp traffic.
WHY: Step 1 proved size reduction (45%) with zero text loss, but reduction is not the claim — better-than-summary continuation is. Without this test a smaller context that answers worse would ship as a win.
APPROACH:
1. Corpus: compaction/fixtures/omp-session-big-20260917.jsonl via compaction/src/omp-adapter.ts. Arm A context = compactMessages() output (see compaction/runs/replay-big-20260917.json; re-derive, do not trust it).
2. Extract the 5 dropped call ids (dump decisions with a tsx one-liner against the real Jev client) and author 3 resume questions answerable ONLY from dropped results, with expected answers quoted from the fixture.
3. Arm B context: one generic condensation of the same transcript (fixed prompt, recorded in receipt; `omp -p`, default model).
4. Resume: one fresh model call per arm, identical prompt (context + questions). Record answers verbatim. Grade substring-match against expected.
BUDGET: ~4 live calls total (Arm A re-derive 1, summary 1, resume 2). State each call in the receipt.
NON-GOALS: No library changes. No new fixtures from other sessions. No prompt-tuning to make an arm win.
ACCEPTANCE: compaction/runs/ab-<date>.json with both contexts' byte sizes, both answer transcripts, per-question grades, and a one-line verdict (A wins / B wins / tie). Verdict must be reproducible from the receipt alone.
RECEIPT: The runs/ab JSON + close reason citing it. Report model names, Jev request count, and TYPESAFE_API_KEY sourcing (env only, never in tree).
close_reason: Receipt compaction/runs/ab-20260917.json; live verdict B wins (A 1/3, B 3/3), four live calls, commit e763fa3.

comments.author: WindyJaguar
comments.text:
VERDICT: B wins.

Scores: Arm A 1/3; Arm B 3/3.
Why: fact recall from dropped results; Arm A abstained honestly on Q1/Q3 rather than hallucinating.

CAVEATS: N=1 transcript, N=3 questions, the summary prompt explicitly instructed preserving exact values (favoring B's tested dimension), and both resumes used one model family. The verdict is reproducible from the receipt but narrow; it is not evidence of general superiority.

FOLLOW-UP (not started; conductor routes next): test threshold sensitivity — 0.5 dropped all early reads; measure what 0.2 keeps and at what context size. Also run a task-continuation variant. Treat both as new experiments, not reinterpretations of this run.

title: Omp hook-surface recon plus thin compaction adapter
description:
WHAT: Determine whether omp's --hook extension surface exposes a pre-compact/compaction interception point, and if so build the thin adapter; if not, document the gap and the fallback.
WHY: The library core is transport-agnostic but the only wired adapter targets Claude Code's session.compact hook. In-harness compaction lives or dies on whether omp offers the equivalent surface.
APPROACH:
1. RECON (read-only): read ~/.omp/agent/extensions/dcg-guard.ts as the API example (DO NOT EDIT — another lane's file; run `am file_reservations conflicts` before touching anything near it), `omp --help` hook flags, any hook topic docs. Name the exact hook point or its absence with file:line evidence.
2. If a pre-compact point EXISTS: write compaction/src/omp-hook.ts mirroring fast-jev-compaction/hooks/fast-jev.ts (transcript in, pruned messages out, passthrough fallback on Jev failure — never throw away context on error), plus deterministic tests with a canned asker (no network) and extension of gate 40.
3. If NO point exists: write compaction/runs/hook-recon-<date>.md naming the gap, the closest available surface, and the recommended fallback (explicit command vs wrapper script). No speculative code.
NON-GOALS: No changes to fast-jev-compaction/. No edits outside compaction/ (+ gate 40 only if building). No live Jev calls for recon; at most 2 to smoke-test an adapter.
ACCEPTANCE: Either (a) adapter + green deterministic tests + gate 40 extended, or (b) recon receipt with file:line evidence that no interception point exists and a named fallback. A bare "no hook found" with no surface survey fails.
RECEIPT: Code + tests, or the hook-recon markdown. Close reason cites it.
close_reason: Adapter path: compaction/src/omp-hook.ts + 12 canned-asker tests (17/17 suite, tsc clean) + receipt compaction/runs/hook-recon-20260917.md (verbatim session_before_compact quotes, L0 claim) + gate 40 extended with passthrough RED arm (gate + both selftests green). Commits be199ce, 00b81ff.

title: Distinct-lineage review of this session's hook + gate substrate
description:
WHAT: get a DISTINCT-LINEAGE review of this session's substrate mutations - githooks/pre-commit (staged-deletion + autofix lanes), githooks/commit-msg (verification-level), the absolute core.hooksPath, and the seven-stage foundation/gates.sh.

WHY: P6 leg 1 exists to refuse exactly what happened here - one lineage (Claude Opus) authored AND graded every one of those changes. REVIEW-PERSONAS.md says so in writing rather than assuming it away. The blast radius is not theoretical: githooks/pre-commit runs on every commit by all three panes in this worktree, and a tool_call-class misfire in a hook is fail-closed. The gates are proven in both directions by MY OWN witnesses, which is the self-grade the rule names.

APPROACH: route to a genuinely different lineage - kimi-k3 (skill://kimi-k3), a Codex-family model, or Gemini - with these questions:
1. githooks/pre-commit: can lane 1 or lane 2 refuse a LEGITIMATE commit shape my six satisfying witnesses do not cover?
2. Is --check-mode autofix the right call, or does flagging-without-fixing just move the friction?
3. 60-staged-deletion-lane.sh: is the trigger witness actually exercising the GIT_INDEX_FILE divergence, or a weaker path?
4. Does any gate stage pass by construction (a check that cannot fail on a real tree)?

ACCEPTANCE: a written review from a named non-Claude lineage, its divergences recorded either as fixes or as argued refusals, and the reviewer_lineage/author_lineage pair recorded in the close_reason. Not satisfied by another Claude pane reading it.

title: Foundry bug: house-gate selftests fail under init.templateDir (needs git-config isolation)
description:
WHAT: report and fix upstream that loop-kit gate selftests which build a throwaway git fixture repo fail on any machine with `init.templateDir` set.

WHY: measured 2026-09-17 on this machine. `init.templateDir = ~/.git-templates` installs the commit-msg verification-level hook into EVERY newly created repo, so a selftest that inits a temp repo and commits plain fixture messages dies at "SELFTEST FAIL: fixture repo setup" - the hook correctly refuses a level-less subject. Discriminating proof:
  commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest                              -> FAIL (fixture repo setup)
  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null ... --selftest -> PASS (3 known-bad flagged, 3 clean controls passed)
So the FIXTURE was broken, not the gate - and every future gate with the same shape inherits the defect. Our wrapper (foundation/gates.d/50-house-gates.sh) already neutralizes the config; the fix belongs upstream so the whole fleet gets it.

ACCEPTANCE: loop-kit gate selftests pass with ambient config on a machine with init.templateDir set - by isolating git config or committing with --no-verify inside the fixture. Verify by running `commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest` with NO env overrides and getting SELFTEST PASS.

title: Route: no oracle row exists for the jev/System One domain in fh oracles
description:
WHAT: get a `jev` / System One domain row into fh's oracle catalogue.

WHY: `fh oracles --json` returns 18 verified domains (http2, markdown, terminal, libc, sqlite, redis, metal_fp, pane_state, video_render, ...) and NONE is jev or System One. Mission 1 of an fh pass is NAME THE ORACLE, and a domain with no row means every other layer grades decoration on an unfalsifiable claim. This lane does have real candidate oracles, already named in GATES.md ## Oracle: TypeSafe's documented response schema, the official system-one-adapter-python differential, evals.typesafe.ai, our foundation/ held-out calibration set, and the jev-1.13 jaggedness catalogue. oracles.tsv is franken-harvest's corpus, so the row is theirs to add.

ACCEPTANCE: `fh oracles --domain jev` (or system_one) returns a verified row naming the external reference and how it is differentially tested. Until then every jev claim in this lane cites its oracle inline from GATES.md ## Oracle.

title: Route: add jev to fh's authoritative target manifest so standards can stamp
description:
WHAT: get this lane into franken-harvest's authoritative five-column target-project manifest so `fh standards stamp` can run here.

WHY: `fh standards check --repo .` returns STANDARDS_NOT_STAMPED ("AGENTS.md carries no standards pointer"), and the fh preflight makes an unstamped repo the FIRST finding of any rigor pass. The stamp is blocked on an input this lane does not own:
  fh standards stamp --repo . --source ~/Developer/franken-harvest/standards --targets <tsv>
refuses with [CANNOT_DETERMINE/SCOPE_MANIFEST_INVALID] "target manifest header is not the authoritative five-column schema", and `grep -rl jev ~/Developer/franken-harvest/receipts/*.tsv` is EMPTY - jev appears in no census. Authoring a TSV locally to satisfy the checker is the SUBSTRATE anti-pattern fh explicitly forbids ("route it; do not hand-roll").

ACCEPTANCE: `fh standards check --repo .` returns code:PASS with a matching payload_content_id, reached by franken-harvest naming/publishing the authoritative manifest and adding a jev row. Not by this lane writing a TSV. Blocked until then.

title: Foundry bug: three stamp-check items score vendored clones as first-party code
description:
WHAT: report that stamp-check's code-surface items count VENDORED third-party clones, producing three false positives in an evaluation-lane repo, and ask for a vendored/ignored-path exclusion or an allowance row.

WHY: this lane's root holds ~20 clones of other people's repos (gitignored by an allowlist). Measured against jev@f80c464:
  p5-autofix        "969 code files present but NO autofix precommit WIRED" - the 969 are almost entirely upstream. Wiring an autofix pre-commit over them would REWRITE OTHER PEOPLE'S CODE.
  rc0-declared-path "a Rust bin crate exists but is undeclared" - the crate is vendored `s1-rs`; it is not our CLI.
  p10-commit-sweep  "[S2-UNRESOLVED-TODO] ... compaction/fixtures/omp-session-20260917.jsonl" - the TODO is inside a RECORDED omp session transcript used as a test fixture; it is data, not a task.
fh doctrine: FALSE_POSITIVE => file the checker bug, do NOT fix the repo to satisfy a wrong check.

ACCEPTANCE: stamp-check either honours the repo's ignore rules when enumerating a code surface, or supports a DELIBERATELY_NOT allowance row carrying owner+reason+dies_when. Verified by re-running `stamp-check.sh --repo /Users/josh/Developer/jev` and seeing those three items PASS or N-A with the reason printed.

comments.author: josh
comments.text: Fourth item for the same report: p12-loop-integrity errors exit 3 ('driver missing') and stamp-check classifies that FAIL, fail-closed. For a repo with NO tick loop that is a false FAIL, not a gap - the correct verdict is N-A, exactly as rc0-declared-path yields N-A when there is no .rust-cli-path AND no [[bin]] crate. Measured on jev@HEAD: 51 PASS / 1 FAIL / 1 PARTIAL / 11 N-A, and the single remaining FAIL is this classification. Ask: a no-driver => N-A path, symmetric with rc0's.
